prompts.v2:
Target node: CWD-1016 目的缓冲区访问长度不正确

This node is only about destination-side capacity mistakes.

Classify as VULNERABLE when any visible destination-side pattern appears:
- fixed local buffer or object field receives a write/copy length larger than its real capacity
- destmax/capacity argument is unrelated to the real destination object
- pointer destination or out-parameter is written with runtime length but there is no trustworthy capacity proof and no local guard
- dst + offset or repeated append writes fail to reduce remaining capacity and can overrun in total
- fixed-size destination receives external length without local destination validation

Do NOT classify as CWD-1016 when:
- only the source/read side is too long -> CWD-1015
- only raw array indexing is wrong -> CWD-1028
- only container/list/vector/map position is wrong -> CWD-1043
- the issue is merely choosing an unsafe wrapper/API without a destination-capacity mismatch

BENIGN when:
- the visible code proves the true destination capacity or remaining space before the write
- safe API plus correct destination bound
- container/array indexing is safe and this is not a destination-length bug

If both source and destination look suspicious, classify as CWD-1016 only when the missing proof is on destination capacity.
If uncertain, output BENIGN.
Return exactly one token: VULNERABLE or BENIGN.
prompts.v4:
Target node: CWD-1016 目的缓冲区访问长度不正确
Target meaning: Destination Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value

Use this strict boundary.

Output VULNERABLE when the visible snippet writes, appends, or copies into a destination whose true capacity is not proven, including these common forms:
- `memcpy_s(dst, len, src, len)` or `strcat_s(dst, len, ...)` where `len` comes from external input, struct field, count, or request size instead of the real destination object size
- destination is a struct field, array field, message tail, nested `aucData`, out-parameter buffer, or pointer returned by `buf + offset`, and the code passes a runtime destmax/count without proving that sub-buffer has that much capacity
- helper/append function takes `(buf_ptr, buf_len*)` or `(dst, remaining_len)` and copies a fixed or source-sized object into it without local proof that the remaining destination space is enough
- source-side checks do NOT save this node: checking `total <= strlen(src)+1` or checking source length alone is still VULNERABLE if destination capacity is unproven
- checking only `len <= MAX_SIZE` is NOT enough unless the visible code also proves the real destination field/buffer capacity is that same size

Do NOT classify as CWD-1016 when:
- there is no destination write at all, for example plain `memcmp`/read-only compare length cases -> not this node
- the real issue is source-side overread -> CWD-1015
- the real issue is raw array indexing -> CWD-1028
- the real issue is container element/iterator access -> CWD-1043

BENIGN only when the visible snippet proves the exact destination capacity or exact remaining destination space before the write.
If destination-capacity proof is missing, lean VULNERABLE.
Return exactly one token: VULNERABLE or BENIGN.
prompts.v5:
Target node: CWD-1016 目的缓冲区访问长度不正确

Judge only destination-capacity proof.

VULNERABLE if any of these are visible:
- destmax is set to the same external/runtime length as copy count instead of the real destination size
- copy/write targets a buffer field, local array, nested struct tail, out buffer, or advanced pointer and the code never proves how much space that destination actually has
- append helper writes into `*buf`, `buf+used`, `ies+offset`, `aucData`, or similar remaining-space destination using caller-provided length but no visible remaining-capacity proof
- the function validates only the source size, payload size, or generic MAX constant, but never validates the actual destination object capacity

BENIGN only if the visible code shows one of:
- real destination size is used directly, such as `sizeof(real_dest)` or exact remaining-space calculation
- a guard proves destination capacity before the write
- the destination is obviously at least as large as the requested write from visible local code

Not this node:
- no destination write at all, especially pure `memcmp`/read-side cases
- source-length bug only -> CWD-1015
- array index OOB -> CWD-1028
- container access OOB -> CWD-1043

When in doubt about destination capacity, do not assume caller guarantees. Choose VULNERABLE.
Return exactly one token: VULNERABLE or BENIGN.
